description: AstroBase is an interactive, browser-based space outpost life-support simulation game designed for students and young space enthusiasts. Space-themed educational content often oversimplifies real mission engineering trade-offs or presents them at a level too complex for young learners. AstroBase makes these trade-offs tangible and fun: players take the seat of Flight Director managing Moon Base Artemis (Shackleton Rim) or Mars Base Ares (Jezero Crater).
summary:
AstroBase is an interactive, browser-based space outpost life-support simulation game designed for students and young space enthusiasts. Space-themed educational content often oversimplifies real mission engineering trade-offs or presents them at a level too complex for young learners. AstroBase makes these trade-offs tangible and fun: players take the seat of Flight Director managing Moon Base Artemis (Shackleton Rim) or Mars Base Ares (Jezero Crater).

Players must balance four interdependent, life-critical systems: Oxygen Circulation, Electrical Power Grid, Hydroponic Food & Water, and Radiation Hull Shielding. Every engineering decision carries real trade-offs: boosting oxygen scrubbers drains electrical batteries; harvesting greenhouse crops consumes water; clearing solar arrays requires astronaut EVA oxygen expenditure. Powered by real-time orbital radar animation, Web Audio API sound synthesis, and dynamic mission events (solar coronal mass ejections, Martian dust storms, micrometeorite punctures), AstroBase empowers students to experience firsthand the decisions that determine whether an extraterrestrial outpost survives.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

AstroBase simulates day-to-day life support operations on the Moon and Mars across sequential mission Sols (days):

• 4 Critical Life-Support Gauges: Live percentage bars and warning klaxons for Oxygen (O2), Electrical Power, Hydroponics/Water, and Radiation Shielding.

• Turn-Based Engineering Directives: Players choose tactical directives each Sol: "Boost Oxygen Scrubbing" (+18% O2, -12% Power), "Harvest Greenhouse Crops" (+16% Food, -10% Power, -6% Water), "Reinforce Regolith Shield" (+20% Shielding, -14% Power), or "Astronaut EVA Solar Maintenance" (+22% Power, -8% O2).

• Dynamic Space Hazards: Simulates realistic NASA deep-space events including Solar Particle Events (CMEs), Martian electrostatic dust storms, cryogenic night shadow dips, and autonomous cargo lander resupplies.

• Animated Radar Canvas: Real-time radar screen tracking the ECLSS dome, solar field, hydroponic greenhouse, and ISRU landing pad.

• In-App NASA Tech Dossier: Educational briefing detailing real flight systems (ECLSS, MOXIE, Kilopower, and regolith 3D printing).

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Makes deep-space life support physics intuitive for school-age students. Teaches conservation of energy, closed-loop recycling, and systems engineering without overwhelming jargon.

3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

Vanilla HTML5, CSS3 responsive grid layout, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas 2D context, and the Web Audio API for custom sound synthesis (zero external audio files or dependencies).

4. CREATIVITY & INNOVATION

Introduces a tactile "trade-off penalty engine" where no single resource can be maximized without sacrificing another, modeling the real thermodynamic constraints of space travel.

5. FACTORS CONSIDERED

Incorporated physical differences between lunar vacuum/cryogenic cold and Martian thin carbon dioxide atmospheres and seasonal dust storms.
